items.title: 68089_John Malachi oral history interview
items.q: I had another place in there where there was a little written interlude for the alto saxophone player. It was kind of in the style of some things that I had heard Willie Smith do with the Jimmy Lunceford band.

ctx.x: Tympany Five. And Louis Jordan was hot as the proverbial firecracker, and he was making a whole lot of money. And there were a lot of musicians that were with Jimmy Lunceford who were disenchanted with what he was doing. Because Jimmy Lunceford, from what I understand, was sort of like a schoolmaster. He had this good band, a very disciplined band, and good musicians. But as far as him giving them any money that they rightfully deserved, he didn't seem to be so willing to do that. So he began to lose people like…

Anyway, Trummy, after having met me in Tommy Miles' band that he had been a former member of... Because whenever that band came in town, they'd come around and see Tommy Miles, and I got to know him. When he left Jimmy Lunceford, he came down to see me, and he knew that I was doing some writing and everything. He told me about this idea that he had about getting this little band together. He spoke about a voicing. where he was going to use trombone, tenor and alto. After hearing our little band down there, he…
